title: An enciphered copy of al-Jawlānī's rhymed-prose riddle in a Mamluk book of ciphers, about 1325-1360 (Penn LJS 51, f. 48r-48v)

documents.shelfmark: University of Pennsylvania, Kislak Center, LJS 51, f. 48r l.8 - 48v l.13 (OPenn images 0084_0100, 0084_0101)
documents.date: correspondence of the volume about 1325-1360 (this project's dating in the corpus notes); Penn dates the manuscript "14--"

plaintext.source: The same riddle is written in clear on f. 21r l.7 - 21v l.2 of the volume, after another encipherment of it (chain 20r.8). It was found after the key was recovered blind.

transcription.source: OPenn master TIFFs 0084_0100 and 0084_0101, by eye; every flagged position re-read at 2-3x (recheck_2x.md)
transcription.notes: Measured with --drop-first and the divider | skipped: 228 signs, 27 labels, 47 dividers. The chain record counted 226 signs by eye and the first transcription 229; the 2x re-read removed two phantom W, added a missed SW and changed one HK to SW.

system.summary: Simple substitution of invented signs for Arabic letters, right to left, with a dotted stem between words.
system.sibling_key: f. 47r key (same sign family) tried and ruled out
system.notes: 27 labels for 25 letters: ya has two labels (AY, O8) and lam two (X, XN, one occurrence); whether these are homophones or variant shapes was not checked. Words may run over a line end.

prior_solution.where: No study of LJS 51 found (corpus prior-art notes; the sibling target's catalogue vetting of 15 Nov 2026: Penn TEI, Digital Scriptorium, DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry's list, web). DECODE has no record of the manuscript. The compiler gives the riddle in clear on f. 21r but writes no solution after this block.

conditions.human_role: None for this block beyond the corpus project's brief (transcribe and rekey every chain of LJS 51).

solution.what: OPenn master TIFFs of ff. 48r and 48v (images 0084_0100, 0084_0101) used for the transcription and crops.
Chain record 48r.8: 19 lines, 226 signs by eye, 51 groups; same sign family as the f. 47r block. Then a labelled transcription (transcription.txt v1): 229 signs, 52 groups.
Applied the f. 47r key (keys_eye/47r.1.json) to the block.

Tested by length and group pattern the verses on 49r l.6-7 (72 letters), the first five verses of the 47r riddle (about 208 letters; the 47r key does not give wa-ma at verse starts) and the compiler's eight answer-verses (about 320 letters).

anneal_sp.py: one-to-one keys, word dividers as spaces, ar-mamluk model, 6 restarts x 40,000 steps, no plaintext given. Restart 1 reached -2.51 per character and read Arabic ('... ahl aslah tathur idha b n al-layl wa-tarhal 'ind al-safah tarmiha ... wa-hiya ma'duda min na'im ahl al-janna ...'); the other five scored -2.64 to -3.24 with partial words.

Identified the annealer's text as the rhymed-prose riddle in clear on f. 21r l.7 - 21v l.2 (plaintext of chain 20r.8). DP alignment with the key re-learned over 6 rounds (verify.py): 218 of 229 signs take their letter (95.2%); the block covers the first 232 of the riddle's 293 letters, to jammalatuhu.

Re-read every flagged position at 2-3x on the masters (recheck_2x.md): five transcription errors and six misplaced dividers corrected (229 -> 228 signs); the OM sign is qaf in both places. With transcription v2 (verify_v2.py): 220 of 228 signs (96.5%) take the key; 3 surplus signs, 7 dropped letters, all scribal slips or places where the cipher corrects the clear copy (tarmiha, yuhmad, al-qisi).
Rule-out (ruleout.txt): the decoded block (v1, 229 signs) against all 206 plaintexts of the book, share of signs in matching runs: 20r.8 0.952, next best 22r.1 0.223, median 0.092.
Prior art for the volume: no study of LJS 51 found; DECODE has no record of it.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 228 tokens, 27 types, ar-mamluk order 4: reading -2.627 per letter; random keys -5.236 (z 5.5); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.841 (mean -2.911, z 5.5); annealer on the real text -2.715. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.627; polyphony 0.0; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.715

outcome.method_basis: The annealer, given only the signs and an Arabic letter model, reached the text of the riddle; the clear copy on f. 21r was matched to it afterwards and used only to check the key and the slips.
outcome.fraction_read_source: transcription.txt decoded with key.json (decode.py): all 228 cipher signs have a value; 220 of them give the letter of the clear copy as recorded (verify_v2.py); the other 8 are scribal slips (emended in reading.md) or the three places where the cipher corrects the record; unit cipher signs
outcome.notes: The block enciphers part of the riddle (to جملته), not all of it; the rest of the clear text is not enciphered here. The cipher corrects the 20r.8 record of the clear copy in three places: ترميها (record توهمها), يحمد (record وخمد[?]), القسي (record العسى[?]).

texts.label: Penn LJS 51, f. 48r l.8 - 48v l.13: the riddle, first 232 letters

reading_review.by: Claude (write-up session, a model's review, not a person's)
reading_review.note: Read as sentences against the clear copy on f. 21r (chain 20r.8) and its translation: every rhymed-prose clause builds; the seven slips are emended in [ ] from the clear copy, and three places follow the cipher against the record of the clear copy.

texts.summary: The first part of a riddle in rhymed prose (the fourth enciphered piece of the series), which the compiler writes in clear on f. 21r: something soft of sides and wide of flanks that visits at night and leaves at dawn, counted among the bliss of Paradise and spread out 'by a permitted contract'. The compiler gives the answer as the raised couches (furush marfūʿa) of Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa. The enciphered copy stops at جملته.
